events.note: Authored for credential-evidence#244 (D3) from the cited provider pages read on 2026-10-05; carrier existence and derivation are provider-documented, the span and value policy are project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-05 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence#244. Question: is the second part of a pipe-joined app-id-and-app-secret access_token value a credential, and is the pair attributed to a family? Options: flag the second part only; flag the whole pair; or leave the case a draft. Decision: flag the second part only (the app ID before the pipe is not in the span), with no attribution of the pair to the app secret or the app access token family beyond the app-secret subject role. Reason: the page names the second part the app secret and the first part the app ID, and documents no format, so the expectation rests on project policy and is not a provider rule. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's instruction.
events.dissent: The page does not say whether the app ID is public, so excluding it from the span asserts nothing about it; a bare-value consumer can still flag a differently shaped pair that the position rule misses, and the pair may be an app access token rather than the app secret.
events.reversingEvidence: A Meta statement that the pair is an access token of its own or that the app ID is confidential, or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes the span.
